entities.summary:
Berchtold Haller (c. 1492–1536) was a leading Reformer of Bern, a preacher whose advocacy of evangelical doctrine helped turn the powerful Swiss city-republic toward Protestantism in the 1520s.

Trained in humanist and theological currents of the Upper Rhine, Haller worked with local magistrates and with allies such as Zwingli’s wider network to replace the Mass and reorganise church order.

Bern’s Reformation mattered beyond the city: its military and diplomatic weight spread Protestant politics across Switzerland and beyond, contributing to the Thirty Years' War and the rise of Calvinism in Europe.
